text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* The bicameral commission aimed at carrying out constitutional reforms agreed on a draft programme of new electoral system, taking into account the centre-left majority favouring a strong prime minister and centre-right opposition backing presidential semi-system (all).

* In an interview, Sergio Cofferati, the head of Italy's biggest labour group CGIL, said prime minister Romano Prodi could not expect to reform the welfare state by only cutting pension spending (Corriere della Sera).

* The prospectus for the third tranche of the privatisation of state-controlled energy group ENI said the group expected its net profit to be higher than 1996. ENI's board also approved of the incorporation of its oil exploration and production unit Agip and said it didn't rule out a merger its natural gas supply, transmission and distribution unit Snam (all).
* Household electrical goods producer Zanussi said it posted 1996 net profit of 175 billion lire, 22 percent down on the previous year, with turnover down 3.5 percent to 5.024 trillion lire (all).
** Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
